titleEn: The Song of the Cid — The last night at Cardeña: Ximena's prayer, the farewells, the road into exile (tirada 18, lines 295–403)
part: Tirada 18 · The last night at Cardeña: Ximena's prayer, the farewells, the road into exile (lines 295–403)

sentences.i: When my Çid, he of Vivar, learned that his company was growing — whereby he would be worth the more — he mounted in haste and rode out to receive them;
sentences.n: Tirada 18 (assonance á) — the Çid welcomes the new men; the term runs short; the last night at San Pedro de Cardeña, Ximena's prayer at matins, the farewells, and the first marches south to the edge of Castile. The line-endings carry a single stressed á (Bivar, valdrá, sonrisar, besar, voluntad, far …), and the endings in á-e count with them — sale, heredades, sabe, madre, cárçel, Calvarie (Calvárie), partes, alguandre, sangre, padres, carne, Fáñez: an unstressed final -e after the stressed á, with or without a consonant after it, does not change the assonance, just as ó and ó-e were one in tiradas 14 and 17. sopo, preterite of saber, 'came to know' (as sopieron, v. 242); lo anticipates the que-clause. el de Bivar, 'he of Vivar', his home (v. 11). quel = que le; conpaña, his following. por que = 'by which, whereby'; valdrá, future of valer: men are a lord's wealth and standing. reçebir los sale = sale a recibirlos: a verb of motion takes the bare infinitive, the pronoun standing loose before it.

sentences.t:
[dont a ojo los ovo], tornós a sonrisar;
lléganle todos, la manol ban besar.
sentences.l:
[whence at eye them he-had], he-turned-himself to smile;
they-come-up-to-him all, the hand-to-him they-go to-kiss.
sentences.i: as soon as he had them in sight, he broke into a smile; they all come up to him and kiss his hand.
sentences.n: The first half of v. 298, [dont a ojo los ovo], is wholly Pidal's restoration, and the line after it he numbers 298b. dont (= donde) is here 'when, as soon as' rather than 'where'; a ojo los ovo, 'had them at eye', within sight (aver 'to have, hold' once more). tornós = tornóse: tornarse a + infinitive, 'to set to, begin'; whether it also means 'smiled again' is not certain. sonrisar = sonreír. lléganle, present after the preterites: tense-mixing. manol = mano + l(e), as at v. 174; ban = van, b for v; ir + infinitive, 'they go to kiss', the hand-kiss of men taking a lord.

sentences.t:
Fabló mio Çid de toda voluntad:
“yo ruego a Dios e al Padre spirital,
vos, que por mí dexades casas e heredades,
enantes que yo muera, algún bien vos pueda far:
lo que perdedes doblado vos lo cobrar.”
sentences.l:
Spoke my Çid with all will:
“I pray to God and to-the Father spiritual,
you, who for me leave houses and inheritances,
before that I die, some good to-you I-may-be-able to-do:
that-which you-lose doubled to-you it to-restore.”
sentences.i: My Çid spoke with all his heart: “I pray to God and to the spiritual Father that before I die I may do you some good — you who are leaving houses and lands for my sake — and restore to you twice over what you lose.”
sentences.n: de toda voluntad, 'with all his will', wholeheartedly. el Padre spirital, 'the spiritual Father', God the Father, set beside Dios in a pious doublet; spirital = espiritual. The speech is built loosely, as speech is: vos is set out first as the people concerned ('you, who …'), and ruego … pueda follows without its que. dexades, present, 'you are leaving'; casas e heredades, houses and inherited lands — the losses of v. 289. enantes que = antes que, with the subjunctive muera. far = fazer, the short infinitive (f- for modern h-). v. 303 is most likely a bare infinitive hanging on the same pueda, 'that I may restore it to you doubled'; cobrar is 'to recover, make good'. That construction is the likeliest reading, not a certain one. lo que perdedes is taken up again by lo.

sentences.t:
Plogo a mio Çid, por que creçió en la yantar,
plogo a los otros omnes todos quantos con él están.
sentences.l:
It-pleased to my Çid, because it-grew in the meal,
it-pleased to the other men all as-many-as with him are.
sentences.i: My Çid was glad that there were more of them at table, and glad too were all the other men who are with him.
sentences.n: plogo, strong preterite of plazer, 'it pleased' (modern plació), used impersonally; por que here is 'because', giving the cause of his pleasure. creçió has no subject expressed: most likely the conpaña of v. 296 — 'it grew', so that more men sat down to the meal — but this is not certain. la yantar, the meal, here feminine (yantar as at v. 285). omnes = hombres (Latin homines). todos quantos, 'all as many as'; están, present, after the preterite.

sentences.t:
Los seys días de plaz[d]o passados los an,
tres an por troçir, sepades que non más.
sentences.l:
The six days of term passed them they-have,
three they-have for to-pass, may-you-know that not more.
sentences.i: Six days of the term are now gone; three remain to pass, and no more, be sure of it.
sentences.n: The plazo is the time the king allowed the Çid to leave his kingdom: six days gone and three to come make nine. plaz[d]o = plazo, the d restored by Pidal (as at v. 212). passados los an = los han pasado: aver + past participle, the participle agreeing with los seys días and set first for weight. an por troçir, 'they have still to pass': aver por + infinitive; troçir = 'to pass, go by'. sepades que non más, 'know that there are no more', present subjunctive of saber, the minstrel speaking to his hearers.

sentences.t:
Mandó el rey a mio Çid aguardar,
que, si después del plazo en su tierral pudies tomar,
por oro nin por plata non podríe escapar.
sentences.l:
Ordered the king to my Çid to-watch,
that, if after the term in his land-him he-could take,
for gold nor for silver not he-would-be-able to-escape.
sentences.i: The king had ordered watch kept on my Çid, so that if he could take him in his land after the term was out, he should not escape for gold or silver.
sentences.n: Mandó … aguardar, 'ordered (men) to watch': aguardar is 'to keep watch on', a mio Çid the man watched. tierral = tierra + l(e), the pronoun glued to the noun, as in manol: 'take him in his land'. pudies = pudiesse, imperfect subjunctive of poder with its -e lost; its subject is the king. podríe, conditional of poder, its subject the Çid: 'he would not be able to escape'. por oro nin por plata, no ransom would buy him off; nin = ni.

sentences.t:
El día es exido, la noch querié entrar,
a sos cavalleros mandólos todos juntar:
“Oid, varones, non vos caya en pesar;
poco aver trayo, dar vos quiero vuestra part.
sentences.l:
The day has gone-out, the night wanted to-come-in,
to his knights he-ordered-them all to-gather:
“Hear, barons, not to-you may-it-fall in grief;
little wealth I-bring, to-give you I-want your part.
sentences.i: The day is gone, and night was coming on; he had all his knights gathered together: “Hear me, barons, let it not grieve you: I bring little wealth, but I mean to give you your share.
sentences.n: es exido, 'has gone out', exir with ser, as Exido es at v. 201. querié, imperfect of querer: querer + infinitive, 'to be about to' (cf. quieren [cr]ebar, v. 235). a sos cavalleros … mandólos: the object named with a and taken up again by los glued to the verb; juntar, 'to gather'. Oid = oíd; varones, 'men, barons', the address to fighting men. non vos caya en pesar, 'let it not fall to you as grief': caya = caiga, present subjunctive of caer. aver here is the noun, 'wealth, goods'; trayo = traigo. part = parte, its -e lost.

sentences.i: Be mindful how you are to do it: in the morning, when the cocks crow, do not linger, but have the horses saddled;
sentences.n: Se[e]d = sed, imperative of seer 'to be', the second e restored by Pidal; me[m]brados, 'mindful', its m restored (menbrada, v. 210, there 'prudent'). devedes = debéis, 'you must'. quando … cantarán: the future in a when-clause, where modern Spanish puts the subjunctive (cuando canten). non vos tardedes, mandedes ensellar: present subjunctives as commands; ensellar, 'to saddle', the horses understood.

sentences.t:
en San Pero a matines tandrá el buen abbat,
la missa nos dirá, de santa Trinidad;
la missa dicha, penssemos de cavalgar,
ca el plazo viene açerca, mucho avemos de andar.”
sentences.l:
in San Pero to matins will-ring the good abbot,
the mass to-us he-will-say, of holy Trinity;
the mass said, let-us-think of riding,
for the term comes near, much we-have of to-travel.”
sentences.i: at San Pedro the good abbot will ring for matins and say us the Mass of the Holy Trinity; and when the Mass is said, let us take to horse, for the term is drawing near and we have far to ride.”
sentences.n: tandrá = tañerá, the future of tañer 'to ring', its vowel dropped and a d grown between n and r (as between l and r in valdrá, v. 296). The Mass de santa Trinidad is a votive Mass, one said for a special intention. la missa dicha, a participle phrase standing alone, 'the Mass once said'. penssemos de cavalgar, hortative subjunctive with pensar de + infinitive, 'let us set about riding' (v. 10). avemos de andar: aver de + infinitive, 'we have to go'; andar is 'to travel, cover ground'.

sentences.t: Qu[o]mo lo mandó mio Çid, assí lo an todos ha far.
sentences.l: As it ordered my Çid, so it they-have all to do.
sentences.i: As my Çid commanded, so all of them must do.
sentences.n: Qu[o]mo = commo, 'as', the o restored by Pidal; the qu- spelling is kept as printed. an … ha far = han a fazer: aver a + infinitive, 'to have to' (as a mover [h]a, v. 169, where the infinitive stands first); here the preposition a is written ha. far, the short infinitive, as at v. 302.

sentences.t:
Passando va la noch, viniendo la man;
a los mediados gallos pienssan de [ensellar].
sentences.l:
Passing goes the night, coming the morning;
at the middle cocks they-think of [to-saddle].
sentences.i: The night wears on and the morning comes; at the middle cockcrow they set about saddling.
sentences.n: Passando va, ir + gerund, 'goes passing'; viniendo, a second gerund with va understood. man = mañana (Latin mane), the short form at the rhyme. los mediados gallos, 'the middle cocks', the cockcrow in the small hours between midnight and dawn — the time the Çid set at v. 316. The rhyme-word [ensellar] is wholly Pidal's restoration, answering mandedes ensellar at v. 317.

sentences.t:
Tañen a matines a una priessa tan grand[e];
mio Çid e su mugier a la eglesia van[e].
sentences.l:
They-ring to matins at a haste so great;
my Çid and his wife to the church go.
sentences.i: They ring for matins in great haste; my Çid and his wife go to the church.
sentences.n: Here the bracketed [e] at the line-end begins, and it runs on through Ximena's prayer (grand[e], van[e], altar[e], mal[e], estas[e], mar[e] …). It is the epic paragogic -e: a line ending in a stressed vowel or a consonant could be sung with an extra unstressed e (as entróv[e], v. 15, in tirada 3). Pidal restores it in these lines; with it they sound á-e like madre and sabe around them. It adds nothing to the sense: grand[e] = grand, van[e] = van. a una priessa tan grand[e], 'with a haste so great'. eglesia = iglesia.

sentences.t:
Echós doña Ximena en los grados delantel altar[e],
rogando al Criador quanto ella mejor sabe,
que a mio Çid el Campeador que Dios le curiás de mal[e]:
sentences.l:
Threw-herself doña Ximena on the steps before-the altar,
praying to-the Creator as-much-as she best knows,
that to my Çid the Campeador that God him should-guard from harm:
sentences.i: Doña Ximena cast herself down on the steps before the altar, praying to the Creator as best she knew how that God might guard my Çid the Campeador from harm:
sentences.n: Echós = echóse, 'threw herself down', the enclitic squeeze. grados, 'steps' (Latin gradus); delantel = delante el. quanto ella mejor sabe, 'as best she knows', present inside the past. In v. 329 the sentence starts one way and starts again: que a mio Çid el Campeador … que Dios le curiás, 'that (as for) my Çid … that God might guard him' — the man prayed for is put first and taken up by le. curiás = curiasse, imperfect subjunctive of curiar 'to guard', its -e lost.

sentences.i: “O glorious Lord, Father who art in heaven, thou madest heaven and earth, and the sea the third; thou madest the stars and the moon, and the sun to give warmth;
sentences.n: Ximena's prayer (vv. 330–365) is a creed told as a story: God's works from the creation through the life, death and rising of Christ, with a litany of those he saved, and only at the end the plea for the Çid — the shape is 'as thou didst save them, save him'. Prayers of this kind are found in the French chansons de geste as well. Ya, vocative 'O'. padre que en çielo estas[e] echoes the opening of the Lord's Prayer. fezist = feziste, 'thou madest', 2nd sg. preterite of fazer with its final -e lost — the form that runs through the prayer (prisist, apareçist, salvest). el terçero, 'the third', the sea after heaven and earth. y = 'and'. pora escalentar[e], 'to warm' (escalentar = calentar).

sentences.i: thou didst take flesh in holy Mary, thy mother; in Bethlehem thou didst appear, as was thy will; shepherds glorified thee and gave thee praise;
sentences.n: prisist, 2nd sg. preterite of prender, 'thou tookest' (cf. priso, v. 110). santa María madre, 'holy Mary (thy) mother'; madre is á-e and fits the assonance with no letter added. Belleem = Bethlehem (Luke 2). f[o] = fue, its o restored by Pidal; veluntad[e] = voluntad, with the paragogic e. ouieron (u for v, as printed) [te] a laudare: aver a + infinitive, hardly more than 'they praised thee'; [te] restored by Pidal; laudare is the Latin-shaped infinitive of loar, its -e printed in roman type.

sentences.i: three kings from Arabia came to adore thee, Melchior and Caspar and Balthasar, and offered thee gold and frankincense and myrrh with willing hearts;
sentences.n: The Magi of Matthew 2: the Gospel gives neither their number nor their names; three kings, and these three names, are later tradition. vinieron adorar, the bare infinitive after a verb of motion, as reçebir los sale at v. 297. [C]aspar, its initial restored by Pidal; Baltasar[e], adorar[e], veluntad[e] with the paragogic e. tus = frankincense (Latin tus). [de] veluntad[e], 'willingly', the de restored by Pidal.

sentences.t:
salvest a Jonás, quando cayó en la mar[e]
salvest a Daniel con sus leones en la mala cárçel,
salvest dentro en Roma a señor san Sebastián,
salvest a santa Susanna del falso criminal;
sentences.l:
thou-savedst Jonah, when he-fell into the sea
thou-savedst Daniel with his lions in the evil prison,
thou-savedst inside in Rome lord saint Sebastian,
thou-savedst holy Susanna from-the false charge;
sentences.i: thou didst save Jonah when he fell into the sea; thou didst save Daniel among his lions in the cruel prison; thou didst save my lord Saint Sebastian in Rome itself; thou didst save holy Susanna from the false accusation;
sentences.n: The litany of rescues, each line opening on salvest = salvaste, 'thou savedst'. Jonah, thrown into the sea, swallowed by the great fish and cast up alive (Jonah 1–2). Daniel, shut in the lions' den — la mala cárçel, 'the evil prison' — and unharmed (Daniel 6); con sus leones, 'with his lions', the ones that shared his pit. Saint Sebastian, the Roman martyr who in the legend survives being shot with arrows; señor san, 'lord saint', a title of reverence. Susanna, falsely accused by two elders and cleared by the young Daniel (Daniel 13 in the Latin Bible); criminal is a noun here, 'criminal charge'. The print has no stop after v. 339. cárçel (á-e) and Sebastián fit the assonance.

sentences.t:
por tierra andidiste treynta y dos años, Señor spirital,
mostrando los miraclos, por en avemos qué fablar:
del agua fezist vino e de la piedra pan,
resuçitest a Lázaro, ca f[o] tu voluntad;
sentences.l:
through earth thou-walkedst thirty and two years, Lord spiritual,
showing the miracles, whereof we-have what to-speak:
of-the water thou-madest wine and of the stone bread,
thou-raisedst Lazarus, for was thy will;
sentences.i: thou didst walk the earth thirty-two years, spiritual Lord, showing the miracles of which we have to tell: of water thou madest wine, and of stone bread; thou didst raise Lazarus, for such was thy will;
sentences.n: andidiste, strong preterite of andar (= anduviste). treynta y dos años, 'thirty-two years', the prayer's own figure. Señor spirital, 'spiritual Lord', the epithet of Padre spirital (v. 300). por en = por ende, 'of which, therefore'; avemos qué fablar, 'we have matter to tell'. Water into wine: the wedding at Cana (John 2). Bread from stone is no Gospel miracle — it is what the devil bids Christ do in the temptation, and he refuses (Matthew 4:3); the prayer counts it among the miracles all the same. Lazarus raised from the dead: John 11. f[o] = fue, restored by Pidal.

sentences.i: thou didst let thyself be taken by the Jews; at the place called Mount Calvary, by name Golgotha, they set thee on the cross, with two thieves beside thee, one on either side: the one is in paradise, but the other did not enter there;
sentences.n: dexeste = dejaste; te dexeste prender, 'let thyself be taken'. do dizen monte Calvarie, 'where they call (it) Mount Calvary', runs on into the next line; Calvarie (Calvárie) counts as á-e. por nombre en Golgotá, 'by name, at Golgotha', the other name of the same place, stressed on its last syllable, as the assonance shows. señas partes, 'one side each', i.e. one on either side (señas, distributive, as señas dueñas, v. 263). The good thief is promised paradise (Luke 23:43). ca is normally 'for, because'; here it can only be read as 'but, whereas', and the sense is uncertain. para[d]iso, the d restored by Pidal.

sentences.t:
estando en la cruz, vertud fezist muy grant:
Longinos era çiego, que nu[n]qua vi[d]o alguandre,
diot con la lança en el costado, dont yxió la sangre,
sentences.l:
being on the cross, power thou-madest very great:
Longinus was blind, who never saw ever,
he-gave-thee with the lance in the side, whence went-out the blood,
sentences.i: while thou wert on the cross thou didst a very great wonder: Longinus was blind, and had never seen at all; he struck thee in the side with his lance, and the blood came out,
sentences.n: vertud is a miracle, an act of power (as vertudes, vv. 48, 218). The soldier who pierced Christ's side (John 19:34) has no name in the Gospel; legend names him Longinus, makes him blind, and has him healed by the blood running down the shaft — the story the next lines tell. nu[n]qua vi[d]o alguandre, 'never saw at all': a double negative, nunca … alguandre ('ever, in any way'); the n and d restored by Pidal; vido = vio. diot = diote, 'struck thee': dar con, 'to strike with'. dont = donde, 'whence'; yxió, preterite of exir, 'came out'. alguandre and sangre are á-e.

sentences.t:
corrió por el astil ayuso, las manos se ovo de untar,
alçólas arriba, llególas a la faz,
abrió sos ojos, cató a todas partes,
en ti crovo al ora, por end es salvo de mal;
sentences.l:
it-ran along the shaft down, the hands himself he-had to smear,
he-raised-them up, he-brought-them to the face,
he-opened his eyes, he-looked to all sides,
in thee he-believed at-the hour, therefore he-is saved from evil;
sentences.i: it ran down the shaft of the lance and wet his hands; he raised them up and brought them to his face; he opened his eyes and looked about him on every side; he believed in thee in that hour, and so he is saved from evil;
sentences.n: corrió has la sangre for subject: the blood ran down the astil, the shaft of the lance; ayuso = 'down' (modern abajo). las manos se ovo de untar: aver de + infinitive as a plain past, 'his hands were smeared'. alçólas, llególas, the pronoun glued on; faz, 'face'. cató, from catar, 'looked'. crovo, strong preterite of creer (= creyó); al ora, 'at that hour'. por end = por ende, 'therefore'; salvo, 'saved', in the Christian sense.

sentences.i: in the tomb thou didst rise again; thou didst go down into hell, as was thy will, break down its gates and lead out the holy fathers.
sentences.n: monumento = 'tomb, sepulchre' (Latin monumentum). [oviste] a resuçit[ar]: aver a + infinitive once more, 'thou didst rise'; the auxiliary and the ending are Pidal's restorations. fust = fuiste, here the preterite of ir, 'thou wentest'. This is the harrowing of hell: between his death and his rising Christ breaks the gates of the underworld and leads out the righteous dead of the Old Testament, the santos padres — the creed's 'he descended into hell', told at length in the apocryphal Gospel of Nicodemus. [cr]ebanteste = quebrantaste, its cr restored (as [cr]ebar, v. 235); saqueste = sacaste. padres, á-e.

sentences.t:
Tú eres rey de los reyes, e de todel mundo padre,
a ti adoro e cre[d]o de toda voluntad,
sentences.l:
Thou art king of the kings, and of all-the world father,
to thee I-adore and I-believe with all will,
sentences.i: Thou art King of kings and Father of all the world; thee I adore, and in thee I believe with all my heart,
sentences.n: The creed proper, in the present tense. rey de los reyes, the title of Revelation 19:16. todel = todo el. a ti adoro, with a before the one adored. cre[d]o = creo, its d restored by Pidal (the Latin credo shows through). de toda voluntad, the Çid's phrase at v. 299.

sentences.t:
e ruego a san Peydro que me ayude a rogar
por mio Çid el Campeador, que Dios le curie de mal.
Quando oy nos partimos, en vida nos faz juntar.”
sentences.l:
and I-pray to saint Peter that me he-may-help to pray
for my Çid the Campeador, that God him may-guard from harm.
Since today ourselves we-part, in life us make to-join.”
sentences.i: and I pray Saint Peter to help me pray for my Çid the Campeador, that God may guard him from harm. Since today we part, grant that we be joined again in this life.”
sentences.n: san Peydro, Saint Peter, patron of the monastery (San Pero de Cardeña); Ximena prayed to him before, at v. 240. ayude, curie, present subjunctives after ruego; que Dios le curie de mal is the narrator's curiás de mal[e] (v. 329) now in her own mouth. Only here, after the long creed, comes the plea, and it is short. oy = hoy; Quando, 'since, now that'. faz, imperative of fazer: en vida nos faz juntar, 'make us join (again) in life' — the en vida of vv. 272 and 280, where husband and wife spoke of parting while they live.

sentences.t:
La oraçión fecha, la missa acabada la an,
salieron de la eglesia, ya quieren cavalgar.
sentences.l:
The prayer done, the mass finished it they-have,
they-went-out of the church, now they-want to-ride.
sentences.i: The prayer made and the Mass ended, they came out of the church, ready now to ride.
sentences.n: La oraçión fecha, a participle phrase standing alone (cf. la missa dicha, v. 320); fecha = hecha. la missa acabada la an = la han acabado: the object named, then taken up by la, the participle agreeing. an (present perfect), salieron (preterite), quieren (present): three tenses in two lines. quieren cavalgar, 'they want to ride', or 'they are about to'.

sentences.i: The Çid went to embrace doña Ximena; doña Ximena kisses the Çid's hand, weeping, not knowing what to do.
sentences.n: ívala = íbala: iva + infinitive, 'went to embrace her', la glued to iva after a doña Ximena has named her. va besar, the same periphrasis in the present; manol, 'his hand', as at v. 298b. llorando de los ojos, the weeping formula (cf. v. 265). que non sabe qué se far, 'so that she knows not what to do'; far = fazer.

sentences.i: And he turned to look at the little girls: “To God I commend you, and to the spiritual Father; now we part — God knows of our meeting again.”
sentences.n: tornólas a catar: tornar a + infinitive, 'turned to look at them' (or 'looked at them again'); the girls named with a, then las. acomiendo = encomiendo, 'I commend', as at v. 256. al Padre spirital, as at v. 300. el ajuntar, the infinitive used as a noun, 'the joining (again)': whether and when they will meet is left to God.

sentences.t:
Llorando de los ojos, que non vi[d]iestes atal,
assis parten unos d'otros commo la uña de la carne.
sentences.l:
Weeping from the eyes, so-that not you-saw such,
thus-themselves they-part ones from others as the nail from the flesh.
sentences.i: Weeping from their eyes — you never saw the like — so they part one from another, as the nail from the flesh.
sentences.n: non vi[d]iestes atal, 'you never saw such', the minstrel turning to his hearers; vidiestes = visteis, its d restored by Pidal; atal = tal. assis = assí se, 'thus (they) themselves'; d'otros = de otros. commo la uña de la carne, 'like the nail from the flesh', a proverbial image of a parting that tears. carne is á-e.

sentences.t:
Myo Çid con los sos vassallos penssó de cavalgar,
a todos esperando, la cabeça tornando va.
sentences.l:
My Çid with the his vassals thought of riding,
for all waiting, the head turning he-goes.
sentences.i: My Çid set out to ride with his vassals; waiting for them all, he keeps turning his head to look back.
sentences.n: Myo, with y, as printed. los sos vassallos, article + possessive. penssó de cavalgar, pensar de again. a todos esperando, 'waiting for all', the a marking persons. la cabeça tornando va, ir + gerund, 'he goes turning his head' — the gesture of the poem's first surviving lines (tornava la cabeça, v. 2).

sentences.i: Then Minaya Álvar Fáñez spoke right fittingly: “Çid, where is your courage? You were born of your mother in a good hour! Let us be on our way; leave this for a time of leisure.
sentences.n: A tan grand sabor: sabor is 'relish, pleasure' (a so sabor, v. 234), and the phrase most likely means 'with such great relish', i.e. very much to the purpose; 'with such deep feeling' is also possible, and the sense is uncertain. Minaya is Álvar Fáñez's standing title (he was hailed at v. 14 as Alvar Fáñez), usually explained as mi + anaya, 'my brother' (Basque anaia); Albar = Álvaro, b for v. Fáñez is á-e. do son, 'where are'; esfuerços, 'strengths', courage. en buen[a] nasquiestes de madre: the birth-form of the formula with ora left unsaid, the a restored by Pidal (as at v. 294); nasquiestes, strong preterite of nasçer, 2nd pl. of respect to one man. esto sea de vagar, 'let this be for leisure': vagar is 'leisure, idle time' — the grief must wait.

sentences.t:
Aun todos estos duelos en gozo se tornarán;
Dios que nos dió las almas, consejo nos dará.”
sentences.l:
Yet all these griefs into joy themselves will-turn;
God who to-us gave the souls, counsel to-us will-give.”
sentences.i: All these sorrows will yet turn to joy; God, who gave us our souls, will give us counsel.”
sentences.n: Aun, 'yet, still', with the future. duelos, 'griefs' (Grande duelo, v. 29). se tornarán, simple future of tornarse, 'to turn into'. consejo, 'counsel', what Ximena asked of the Çid at v. 273: help and a way through.

sentences.t:
Al abbat don Sancho tornan de castigar,
commo sirva a doña Ximena e a las fijas que ha,
e a todas sus dueñas que con ellas están;
bien sepa el abbat que buen galardón dello prendrá.
sentences.l:
To-the abbot don Sancho they-turn of to-instruct,
how he-should-serve to doña Ximena and to the daughters that she-has,
and to all her ladies who with them are;
well may-know the abbot that good reward of-it he-will-take.
sentences.i: They turn back to give the abbot don Sancho his charge: how he is to serve doña Ximena and the daughters she has, and all her ladies who are with them; and well may the abbot know that he will have good reward for it.
sentences.n: tornan de castigar: castigar here is 'to instruct, admonish', not 'to punish'; tornar de + infinitive, 'to turn (back) to doing'; the subject, the Çid and his men, is unnamed. sirva, present subjunctive, 'how he is to serve'. las fijas que ha, 'the daughters she has', aver as 'to have'. sepa, present subjunctive as command, 'let him know'. galardón, 'reward'; dello = de ello; prendrá = prenderá, future of prender 'to take', its e dropped. The Çid paid for their keep at v. 253; this is a promise of more.

sentences.t:
Tornado es don Sancho, e fabló Albar Fáñez:
“Si viéredes yentes venir por connusco ir, abbat,
dezildes que prendan el rastro e pie[n]ssen de andar,
ca en yermo o en poblado poder nos [han] alcançar.”
sentences.l:
Turned-back is don Sancho, and spoke Albar Fáñez:
“If you-should-see people come for with-us to-go, abbot,
tell-them that they-take the track and think of travelling,
for in wilderness or in settled-land to-be-able us [they-will] to-overtake.”
sentences.i: Don Sancho has turned back, and Álvar Fáñez spoke: “If you see men coming to go with us, abbot, tell them to follow our track and ride on, for in wild country or in settled they will be able to overtake us.”
sentences.n: Tornado es, ser + participle with a verb of motion, 'has turned back' (as Exido es, v. 201). viéredes, future subjunctive of ver in an open condition. connusco = con nosotros, the fused form (cf. convus[c]o, v. 168). dezildes = decidles, imperative + les with -dl- turned to -ld- (as prestalde, v. 118). prendan el rastro, 'take up the track'; pie[n]ssen de andar, its n restored by Pidal. poder nos [han] alcançar is the split future (= nos podrán alcanzar), nos tucked between infinitive and aver; [han] restored by Pidal. yermo, wilderness; poblado, settled country.

sentences.t:
Soltaron las riendas, pie[n]ssan de andar;
çerca viene el plaz[d]o por el reyno quitar.
sentences.l:
They-loosed the reins, they-think of travelling;
near comes the term for the kingdom to-quit.
sentences.i: They slackened the reins and set off on their way; the term for leaving the kingdom is drawing near.
sentences.n: Soltaron las riendas, the gesture of departure (cf. sueltan las riendas, v. 10); pie[n]ssan, present beside the preterite, its n restored by Pidal. por el reyno quitar, 'for quitting the kingdom', the object set before the infinitive; quitar = 'to leave' (as quitaremos el reynado, v. 211). plaz[d]o, the d restored by Pidal.

sentences.i: My Çid came to lie at Spinaz de Can; great numbers of men gather to him there that night from every side. Next morning he sets out to ride.
sentences.n: Pidal prints v. 395 before v. 394, so that the gathering falls on the night at Spinaz de Can; his print order is followed here and his numbers are kept. yazer = yacer, 'to lie, pass the night'. Spinaz de Can, literally 'Dog's Spine' (espinazo de can), the first night's halt, kept as printed. sele = se le, printed as one word: se acojen, 'gather, come in', le, 'to him'; essa noch, 'that night'. partes is á-e. Otro dia mañana, 'the next day in the morning', dia without accent as printed; pienssa de cavalgar, pensar de once more.

sentences.i: The loyal Campeador is going out of the land: on his left San Esteban, a good city; he passed by Alcobiella, which is already the end of Castile;
sentences.n: Line 398 is not here: Pidal prints it in tirada 19, so this unit runs from 397 straight to 399, with his numbers kept. Ixiendos va = va ixiéndose, ir + gerund of exir, se glued on: 'is going out'. leal, 'loyal', the epithet the poem gives the Campeador even in exile. de siniestro, 'on the left'. Sant Estevan is San Esteban de Gormaz on the Duero; çipdad = ciudad. Alcobiella, where Castile ends: fin, 'end, boundary'; es ya, 'is already'.

sentences.t:
la calçada de Quinea ívala traspassar,
sobre Navas de Palos el Duero va passar,
a la Figueruela mio Çid iva posar.
sentences.l:
the road of Quinea he-went-it to-cross,
over Navas de Palos the Duero he-goes to-cross,
at the Figueruela my Çid went to-lodge.
sentences.i: he crossed the highroad of Quinea; at Navas de Palos he crosses the Duero; at La Figueruela my Çid went to lodge.
sentences.n: calçada, 'paved road', most likely a stretch of an old Roman road; la calçada de Quinea is taken up by la in ívala traspassar, 'went to cross it' (as ívala abraçar, v. 368). sobre Navas de Palos, 'at Navas de Palos', where he crosses the Duero. va passar, iva posar: ir + infinitive as a plain past, the present between two imperfects. posar, 'to lodge, halt' (as posó, v. 59). la Figueruela, 'the little fig-tree'. These places are given as printed; not every one of them can be located with certainty.

sentences.t: Vánssele acogiendo yentes de todas partes.
sentences.l: Go-themselves-to-him gathering peoples from all parts.
sentences.i: From every side men keep coming in to join him.
sentences.n: Vánssele = vanse + le, 'they go (themselves) to him', with ir + gerund acogiendo: a steady stream of men. The tirada ends as it began (v. 296), on the Çid's growing company; partes is á-e, as at v. 395.
